utterance: The EFS file system `my-product` is already up in the account, but it has no file system policy on it at all, so the account-wide default applies and anything that can reach it may mount and write it over a plain connection. Put a system policy on that file system: allow `elasticfilesystem:ClientMount` and `elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite` to AWS principals, on that file system, and only when the connection is TLS. Nothing can reach it either, so give it a mount target in the account's default VPC while you are there.

main.responsibility: owns the application's data and how it is stored and laid out
main.intent: the pre-existing EFS file system my-product carries a file system policy whose statement allows elasticfilesystem:ClientMount and elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite to AWS principals on that file system under a condition requiring aws:SecureTransport to be true, and the file system has a mount target in the account's default VPC
